sourceBindings.text: Dryland farming problems are not all the same. Use the plot's actual texture, organic matter, salt test method, water analysis and profile to distinguish lack of water from difficulty taking up water.

Explain how limited moisture, low organic input, texture, weak structure, alkaline conditions and a verified carbonate-cemented layer can affect an actual dryland soil, without declaring every desert hot, sandy, saline or caliche-bearing.

Differentiate physical water shortage, salt-induced osmotic difficulty of uptake, nutrient imbalance and possible ion toxicity; trace salt input, evaporation, leaching and drainage in a root-zone diagram.
Read the 10 m × 10 m sandy-loam scenario with 0.8% organic matter and EC 3.5 dS/m, ask which EC test and water analysis produced the data, and apply only a table with a matching method and units.

sourceBindings.text: Aridisol
A soil order tied to an aridic moisture regime and diagnostic profile features, not merely a hot or sandy location.
soil organic matter (OM)
Decomposed living-origin material that can affect soil structure, moisture storage and nutrient cycling.
salinity
Concentration of dissolved salts in soil water, interpreted using an explicitly stated sampling and test method.
electrical conductivity (EC)
A measure associated with dissolved salts; values from different soil-extract or water methods are not interchangeable.
ECe
Electrical conductivity of a saturated soil-paste extract, reported for comparison with a table explicitly based on that method and temperature.
ECw
Electrical conductivity of irrigation water, a different measurement from soil ECe.
physiological drought
Difficulty taking up water because dissolved salts lower the soil solution's water potential even while water is present.
leaching
Downward transport of dissolved salts with water below the root zone when suitable water and drainage permit it.
caliche
Calcium-carbonate accumulation that can form a cemented soil layer and restrict roots or water movement if confirmed.
mulch
A cover placed on soil surface to influence evaporation, temperature and erosion; its choice and depth need site assessment.
halophyte
A plant adapted to relatively saline conditions; the label alone does not select a crop for a specific farm.
